abstract: Creative Boom's flagship State of the Creative Industry 2026 survey (June 29, 2026) of 882 creative professionals (UK/US-weighted; 43% with 10+ years experience): nearly 47% of self-employed creatives earn <£30,000/year (vs UK median £39,039). 69% experienced burnout in past 12 months (77% mid-career, 74% early-career). 86% use AI tools but only 10% believe AI's overall impact on the industry is positive; 58% see it as mixed, 28% straightforwardly negative.
keyFindings: 47% of self-employed creatives earn <£30,000/year (below UK median £39,039)
69% experienced burnout in past 12 months (mid-career highest at 77%)
50% feel less financially secure than a year ago; 38% considering a job change; 7.5% planning to leave the industry
86% use AI tools; only 10% think AI's industry impact is positive, 58% mixed, 28% negative
'Creatives aren't refusing to use AI; they're adopting it because they feel they have to'
methodology: Online survey of 882 creative professionals worldwide, UK/US-weighted, fielded by Creative Boom in first half of 2026.
qualifiers: Sample skews UK; Creative Boom audience is self-selecting toward independent creatives who consume industry media. Survey captures sentiment and self-reported earnings, not observed platform data.
